1.explanation:
• sprite-selector-item.jsx (component): Passes a `disable={props.preventContextMenu}` prop to the ContextMenuTrigger. If this prop remains true, the custom menu never re-appears and the browser’s native menu shows instead.
• sprite-selector-item.jsx (container): Computes `preventContextMenu` from `this.dragRecognizer.gestureInProgress()`. Its `handleDragEnd` resets only the Redux drag state and `noClick` flag but never explicitly resets the recognizer’s internal gesture state at the right time, so `gestureInProgress()` can stay true after dragging.
• drag-recognizer.js: Implements `gestureInProgress()` and `reset()`. Because the container relies on `gestureInProgress()` to re-enable context menus, any mismatch between when `reset()` is called here and when the UI stops dragging will leave the context menu disabled. Adjusting where/when `reset()` is invoked (or overriding `preventContextMenu`) in these files will restore the duplicate menu after a drag.
1.bug_scenario: In the first screenshot, the user right-clicks on a sprite in the selector and the Scratch-GUI “duplicate / export / delete” context menu appears as expected. In the second (GIF) sequence, the user drags the same sprite to a new position (i.e. reorders it), then right-clicks again—but instead of the Scratch custom menu, the OS’s native context menu appears. In other words, after finishing a drag operation, the GUI’s context‐menu trigger remains “disabled,” so the native menu takes over.
